summary: Twelve comment-endorsed developer tools, media tools, books, hardware, and AI projects from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: vphone-cli
items.source_story_title: Boot a Virtual iPhone via Apple's Virtualization.framework
items.summary: A command-line tool for booting virtual iPhones with Apple's virtualization stack.
items.why_included: A regular user praised it for app testing and highlighted agent control through vphone-mcp.
items.evidence: The commenter uses the project regularly for app testing and says its MCP companion can control the virtual phone.

evidence_sources.author: thomc
evidence_sources.excerpt: Fantastic project, I use it regularly to test apps and there is a vphone-mcp which allows agents to control it, take screenshots and navigate the UI!

items.name: NUO-STEMS 4
items.source_story_title: StemDeck, a free, open-source and local AI stem separator
items.summary: A music stem separator that integrates its output with major DJ software.
items.why_included: The recommendation was explicit and tied to a practical DJ-software integration advantage.
items.evidence: The commenter recommends NUO-STEMS for DJ use because it integrates with DJ software.

evidence_sources.author: Stitch4223
evidence_sources.excerpt: For dj use I recommend Nuo Stems, as it integrates with dj software.

items.name: OpenVINO AI Plugins for Audacity
items.source_story_title: StemDeck, a free, open-source and local AI stem separator
items.summary: Local AI effects for Audacity, including music separation and transcription workflows.
items.why_included: A firsthand user specifically reported being happy with its stem-separation results.
items.evidence: The commenter says Audacity can perform this task through the OpenVINO plugins and reports good results.

evidence_sources.author: tlahtinen
evidence_sources.excerpt: Audacity can also do this through the OpenVINO plugins and I've been happy with its results

items.name: The Literature of Ancient Sumer
items.source_story_title: Does the Sumerian King List Align with Paleoclimate Events?
items.summary: A substantial translated anthology spanning Sumerian myths, hymns, laments, and poetry.
items.why_included: It was the first title in a direct, detailed reading recommendation from an enthusiastic reader.
items.evidence: The commenter recommends the anthology and highlights its unusually broad range of Sumerian writing.

evidence_sources.author: krzs9
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Literature of Ancient Sumer - Jeremy Black. It is a quite substantial anthology, has myths, hymns, laments, royal praise poetry, proverbs, literary debates, etc.

items.name: Myths from Mesopotamia
items.source_story_title: Does the Sumerian King List Align with Paleoclimate Events?
items.summary: Stephanie Dalley's translations of Gilgamesh and other major ancient Mesopotamian myths.
items.why_included: The reader called it one of their most treasured books after buying it for Gilgamesh.
items.evidence: The commenter bought it for Gilgamesh, loved the remaining texts, and calls it deeply treasured.

evidence_sources.author: krzs9
evidence_sources.excerpt: Myths from Mesopotamia - Stephanie Dalley. I bought this for Gilgamesh, loved the rest of it too. One of my most treasured books.

items.name: Weavers, Scribes, and Kings
items.source_story_title: Does the Sumerian King List Align with Paleoclimate Events?
items.summary: A comprehensive history of Mesopotamia told through rulers, workers, and scribes.
items.why_included: The reader named it their favorite comprehensive history of Mesopotamia.
items.evidence: The commenter calls it their favorite comprehensive Mesopotamian history and praises its treatment of scribal life.

evidence_sources.author: krzs9
evidence_sources.excerpt: Weavers, Scribes, and Kings - Amanda Podany. Not Sumerian literature, but my favorite comprehensive history book covering all of Mesopotamian history.

items.name: BrainAural
items.summary: A browser-based sound generator for immersive, experimental, and ambient listening.
items.why_included: The commenter used it to make an improvised album and called it a really cool tool.
items.evidence: The commenter identifies the second linked tool, BrainAural, as one they used for an improvised album.

evidence_sources.author: ynac
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used the second tool for an improvised album.  Really cool tool.

items.name: dockur/windows
items.source_story_title: Kumander Linux – A Linux Distro with a Windows 7 Desktop
items.summary: A Docker-packaged Windows virtual machine for running Windows applications on Linux.
items.why_included: A Linux user reports it works reliably for the occasional Excel and Word requirement.
items.evidence: The commenter uses one container to run a Windows VM and says it works like a charm for Office apps.

evidence_sources.author: zazuke
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use a single Docker container [1] to run a full VM on Linux, and it works like a charm for Excel and Word when I still need them.

items.name: Keynote: Built in Super Heroes
items.source_story_title: Time complexity of operations on Python's built-in types
items.summary: David Beazley's practical talk on solving data tasks with Python's built-ins.
items.why_included: A commenter directly called it a great talk for data analysis and quick operations.
items.evidence: The commenter recommends David Beazley's talk on using Python built-ins for data work.

evidence_sources.author: alexpotato
evidence_sources.excerpt: Dave Beazley has a great talk about using Python built ins [0] for data analysis and other quick operations.

items.name: Galaxium
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Galaxium, an experimental WebGPU space explorer
items.summary: An experimental WebGPU universe explorer with smooth navigation and rich space visuals.
items.why_included: Independent commenters praised its polish, performance, and visual quality despite minor navigation issues.
items.evidence: A fellow simulation builder calls Galaxium polished and impressive.

evidence_sources.author: andrewchilds
evidence_sources.excerpt: Galaxium is really polished and impressive. Well done!

items.name: Tencent Hy4 preview
items.summary: Tencent's open-weight mixture-of-experts model for coding and general productivity tasks.
items.why_included: A substantial Hy3 user expressed enthusiasm for the new model while noting its predecessor's speed weakness.
items.evidence: The commenter used Hy3 extensively and is excited about Hy4, with serving speed as the main inherited concern.

evidence_sources.author: vcryan
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used Hy3 quite a bit for the type of tasks it was suited for. Excited about this. My one concern over Hy3 was speed.

items.name: Creality Ender-3 V2
items.summary: An affordable desktop FDM printer that can double as a simple pen plotter.
items.why_included: A frequent owner called it a great little printer and was considering another Ender.
items.evidence: The commenter owns and often uses an Ender 3 V2, describing it as a great small printer.

evidence_sources.author: codazoda
evidence_sources.excerpt: I own an Ender 3 V2, which is a great little printer. I use it often and am considering a newer Ender because I want a larger print bed.
